newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Oct 1.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BRITISH GAS ENERGY TAG MAY TOP 2 BILLION POUNDS

City analysts believe that British Gas Energy, the trading company being sold off from British Gas next year, could be worth almost 2 billion pounds stg, which is almost double the value put on the business by Clare Spottiswoode, the industry regulator. The increased valuation comes on the basis of a deal to sell the British Gas trading business in Scotland, Northumberland and Cumbria to Hydro Electric, the electricity supplier.
-- MERSEY WINS 100 MILLION POUNDS PORT CONTRACT IN ARGENTINA

As demonstrators marked the first anniversary of an industrial dispute with a mass picket outside Mersey Docks' Liverpool headquarters, the company, with Clarke Chapman it's partner, announced a 100 million pounds stg contract with Argentina's biggest steelmaker to operate and develop a major private port in the country. The deal is the first with Argentina to be backed by the Export Credits Guarantee Department since the Falklands conflict.
-- MINISTERS COMPLETE 54 MILLION POUNDS HMSO SALE

The completion of the 54 million pounds stg sale of Her Majesty's Stationary Office to National Publishing was announced by the government last night. National Publishing, a consortium backed by venture capital group Electra Fleming hope to make the organisation a more competitive and efficient business. It is thought that between 500 and 1,000 of the 2,600 jobs are threatened by the buy-out.
THE TIMES
-- EUROTUNNEL SAVED FROM INSOLVENCY

Eurotunnel are close to a refinancing deal after a marathon weekend of talks with its bankers. Shares in the Channel Tunnel operator were suspended on the London, Paris and Brussels stock markets yesterday, pending an announcement, and although the company refused to make any further comment, the weekend negotiations are thought to have removed the key stumbling blocks that were standing in the way of refinancing. An announcement on a deal is expected before the end of next week.
-- BRITANNIC TO BACK REFUGE MERGER PLAN

Refuge Assurance and United Friendly's proposed merger looks increasingly likely to go ahead after two of Refuge's major investors decided to back the deal. Britannic, who have a 10 per cent stake were initially concerned that shareholders were being short-changed in the deal, announced yesterday that it would vote through the proposals. Prudential who have 6 per cent, are believed to have reached the same decision after details of an improved offer was published yesterday.
-- HOUSE PRICES UP 7 PER CENT IN PAST YEAR SAYS NATIONWIDE

The latest survey by Nationwide Building Society shows that house prices rose nearly 7 per cent over the past year. Prices were up 1.4 per cent in September, compared with 1.4 per cent in August. Britain's largest mortgage lender, the Halifax is also expected to report that house prices are 5 per cent higher than they were a year ago, when it publishes its monthly index today.
THE GUARDIAN
-- HOLIDAY INN'S CHIEF CHECKS OUT IN A HURRY

The president and chief executive of Holiday Inn resigned last night. Tim Lane, who only held the post for seven months, is likely to receive a seven-figure compensation payment. Bass who own Holiday Inn, said Mr Lane had resigned because of fundamental differences over management. City analysts suggested that Bass had effectively prompted the resignation to avoid other senior managers resigning in protest over Mr Lane's management style.
-- WORLD BANK PLANS POVERTY WATCH

A new watchdog is to be set up by the World Bank to monitor the social effect of its development programmes. The move is to counter claims that its policies are failing the world's poorest people. A report from a task group on social development has been approved by the bank's central policy committee. The paper recommends 4 million pounds stg being put into a Social Learning Group whose role would be to assess the effect of all bank policies on inequality, poverty and the gender gap.
-- LANG SAYS FIRMS WOULD PAY DEAR FOR LABOUR EURO PLAN

By committing Labour to the European Social Chapter on working conditions, Tony Blair has effectively signed a blank cheque on behalf of British companies according to Ian Lang, the Trade and Industry Secretary. Mr Lang, speaking at the launch of a government booklet setting out its opposition to the Social Chapter, warned that the commitment could cost British industry billions of pounds stg.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- WORLD-WIDE SHAKE-UP OF ROTHSCHILD DYNASTY

A big reorganisation of Rothschild is poised to be announced, and will be part of a long awaited management shake-up and will mark a step towards integrating the banking dynasty's world-wide businesses. Baron David de Rothschild is to chair a new group investment banking committee, that is to co-ordinate the family's corporate finance businesses in London, Paris, the rest of continental Europe, Hong Kong, Singapore, Australia, North America and Latin America.
-- HILL DISPUTE COSTS GRAND MET 36 MILLION POUNDS

Brent Walker is to receive a settlement of 36 million pounds stg from Grand Metropolitan GMET over the price the leisure group paid for the William Hill bookmaking chain in 1989. The dispute centered on the profitability of William Hill at the time of the acquisition, which Brent Walker claimed was lower than Grand Met warranted. The decision by the independent arbitrator from the accountants Arthur Andersen opens the way to the final dismemberment of Brent Walker which has been under a mountain of debt since the acquisition of William Hill.
-- RANK SELLS ITS ENGINEERING INTERESTS FOR 72 MILLION POUNDS
Rank Organisation started its planned 300 million pounds stg disposal programme yesterday with the sale of Rank

Precision Industries to Schroder Ventures, for 72 million pounds stg. The proceeds of the sale will help pay for the Tom Cobleigh pub chain which Rank agreed to buy last week. Rank's focus is on leisure retailing and film and entertainment services, RPI's engineering businesses are not part of its strategy. Last month they unveiled plans to dispose of 300 million pounds stg of peripheral assets over the coming two years. BMC+44-171-377-1742
